Why the Quran is from God

The preserved word

The Quran says God guards it. History adds an early settled text, recited ever since.

The Quran says God sent down the Reminder and will guard it. For a believer, that is a promise. For anyone else, history adds this: tradition dates the standard written text to the caliph Uthman, about 650 CE. It has long been learned by heart and recited. The early manuscripts largely conform to it, their differences are recorded, and anyone can look.

﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَـٰفِظُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, it is We who sent down the message [i.e., the Qur’ān], and indeed, We will be its guardian.

Quran · Al-Hijr 15:9

﴿لَّا يَأْتِيهِ ٱلْبَـٰطِلُ مِنۢ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَلَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِۦ ۖ تَنزِيلٌ مِّنْ حَكِيمٍ حَمِيدٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; [it is] a revelation from a [Lord who is] Wise and Praiseworthy.

Quran · Fussilat 41:42

﴿أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَرْتِيلًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Or add to it, and recite the Qur’ān with measured recitation.

Quran · Al-Muzzammil 73:4

You might ask

QuestionHas not one letter ever changed?
AnswerHand copies vary in small points of spelling, and these are recorded openly. The standard copy, which tradition dates to Uthman about 650, has been learned by heart in every generation since.Quran · Al-Hijr 15:9
QuestionAren't there several different readings?
AnswerYes, several recognised ones, each taught through its own chain of teachers. They are one Quran, with differences that mostly concern pronunciation, vowelling and small points of wording.Quran · Al-Muzzammil 73:4
QuestionCan a book vouch for itself?
AnswerNo, and this app does not ask it to. The verse is the Quran's own claim. The history stands apart from it, open to scholars of every background.Quran · Al-Hijr 15:9

The promise is for faith. The history is open. Come and look at both.
